_comment: Sample macrowhisper config for the VoiceInk bridge. Copy to
~/.config/macrowhisper/macrowhisper.json and restart the service.
watch: a DEDICATED directory, never ~/superwhisper. If you ever install
Superwhisper for real, the bridge writing into its recordings folder would
interleave synthetic and genuine recordings.
clipboardBuffer is raised from its 5.0 default to 60.0 ON PURPOSE. macrowhisper
captures pre-recording clipboard context when the recording folder APPEARS
(RecordingsFolderWatcher.swift:441-443), looking back clipboardBuffer seconds
(ClipboardMonitor.swift:1139-1152). Under Superwhisper the folder appears when
recording STARTS; under the bridge it appears when dictation ENDS. So with the
5s default, any dictation longer than 5 seconds loses its pre-recording
clipboard entirely. 60s covers a normal dictation. This does not fix
{{selectedText}}, which still reflects post-dictation state.
moveTo .delete keeps the watch directory from growing without bound. Set it to
'.none' while debugging so you can inspect the generated meta.json files.
simEsc is forced to false ON PURPOSE, and this one destroys user data if you get
it wrong. macrowhisper defaults it to TRUE and, before pasting, posts a literal
Escape keypress to the system-wide HID event tap
(Accessibility.swift:477-494, simulateKeyDown key 53). Under Superwhisper that ESC
dismisses Superwhisper's own recording window. Under this bridge there is no such
window, so the ESC goes straight into whatever app you are typing in. Measured
2026-08-08: dictating into a ProtonMail compose window CLOSED THE DRAFT, and the
paste then had nowhere to land. Any app where ESC means cancel, close, or discard
is exposed. Leave this false.
The url actions below are voice-triggered, and voice triggers are PREFIX-ANCHORED:
macrowhisper builds '^(?i)' + the escaped pattern (TriggerEvaluator.swift:205), so
the phrase must be the FIRST thing in the dictation. '|' separates alternatives and
each is anchored independently, which is why every entry lists both 'ask <site>' and
the bare word: with only the bare word, the natural 'ask youtube best pizza' would
not match and would fall through to the default action with no error at all.
Matching is a raw prefix, not a word boundary, so 'googled' also fires 'google' and
searches for the leftover 'd the answer'. Use a '==regex==' trigger if that matters,
remembering that raw regex disables the automatic prefix stripping.
URL actions get URL-encoding applied to {{swResult}} automatically, so spaces and
punctuation in a dictation are safe there.
NOTE ON THESE COMMENT BLOCKS: a '_comment' key is only safe at the TOP LEVEL or
INSIDE an individual action object. Do NOT add one as a key of 'inserts', 'urls',
'shortcuts', 'scriptsShell' or 'scriptsAS': those decode as [String: Action]
(AppConfiguration.swift:980), so a comment key there fails to decode and takes the
WHOLE config down with it. Unknown keys inside an action object are ignored, which
is why markerLog's own _comment below is fine.
Headless debugging action. Set defaults.activeAction to 'markerLog'
instead of 'autoPaste' to verify the bridge without needing a focused
text field or Accessibility permissions. This is how Gate 1 was proven.
{{swResult}} is in DOUBLE quotes and must stay that way in any shell or
AppleScript action you write. macrowhisper escapes a shell placeholder
with escapeShellCharacters, which covers backslash, double quote,
backtick and dollar, but NOT the single quote, because it assumes a
double-quoted context. In single quotes an ordinary apostrophe ends the
string early: the dictation is lost, or the rest of your words are run
as shell commands. This file shipped single quotes until 2026-08-17.
